title: Prow SLO: Tail-Latency Playbook and Cost Projection (NorthStar Telemetry POC)
summary: Working playbook for the NorthStar Telemetry POC focused on meeting a 200ms p95 generation SLO for short-response queries while bounding cost per 1k requests. Includes environment description, test methodology, measured latency/throughput/cost across variants, and operational recommendations to hit SLOs under bursty traffic.
objective: Validate deployment patterns and configuration knobs that can reliably keep p95 <= 200ms for short prompt class (<= 128 toks) and p99 <= 800ms for mixed long-form requests while providing a 20–40% lower unit-cost than current NorthStar on-prem baseline.
background: NorthStar Telemetry (edge data ingestion vendor) needs an inference stack for realtime enrichment: majority short completions (status codes, short labels), 10% medium (200-600 tokens), 2% long diagnostic summarization. Customer is evaluating Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private migration. This doc captures the POC benchmarking artifacts and pragmatic runbook items.
test_environment: Hosted (Redwood API) in us-west1; Dedicated pool: 4xA100-80GB with 32 concurrency pool; Private: single H100-80GB in customer-edge rack (net isolated). Models tested: open-llm-3-base (fp16), open-llm-3-int4 (quantized), and open-llm-3-small (fast lower-cost variant). SDK: ruby/py harness with synthetic and replay workloads derived from NorthStar production traces (anonymized).
workload_profiles: Short-primary: 75% traffic, median token=34, tail token=120
Burst pattern: 30s microbursts of 600 rps every 7 minutes (simulates batch uploads)
Cold-starts: 1 in 1,000 requests to simulate inactive model shard wakes
methodology: Replay trace-driven load using Redwood load harness. Each configuration run for 60 minutes after a 15-minute warmup. Metrics collected at 1s granularity. We exercised routing policies: strict-latency (favor small model), cost-aware (fallback to quantized), and balanced (default). We measured with and without KV/prefix caching, and with two batching heuristics: fixed small-batches vs continuous batching. Cost estimated from per-minute infra pricing and token consumption recorded by harness.
results_summary: Key numeric summary below — short-class SLOs achievable with combined optimizations. Tradeoffs: lowest-cost setup increases p99 tail substantially during microbursts. Dedicated pool with warm pools + continuous batching provided the best p95 headroom while costing ~28% less than private H100 baseline when amortized at expected QPS.
measurements: Config, p50(ms), p95(ms), p99(ms), throughput(req/s), avg GPU util(%), cost_per_1k(USD)
Hosted fallback strategy (small model for short class), 22, 120, 290, 1180, 55, 12.8
key_findings: 1) Tail behavior dominated by two factors: microburst queuing and cold KV cache misses — prefix caching reduced p95 by ~15–25% for short requests.

2) Continuous batching on Dedicated pools increases throughput and lowers cost per 1k while slightly improving p50; however, it can exacerbate p99 under bursty arrival curves unless concurrency caps are tuned.
3) Quantized model (int4) gives larger cost wins on Dedicated but requires careful validation for medium/long quality; acceptable for short-class production routing.

4) Private single-node H100 provides low p50 and predictable p95 for evenly distributed load, but cost-per-1k is sensitive to utilization — inefficient for spiky workloads unless overprovisioned or paired with burstable hosted fallback.
5) The fastest path to hitting NorthStar's p95 <=200ms SLO is: dedicated pool + prefix cache + routing short traffic to small/speed-optimized model + conservative concurrency caps.
6) Fallbacks: enabling hosted fallback for overflow traffic reduces error rates and saturated tails but increases unit-cost on overflowed requests — build cost dashboards to track overflow billing.
7) Cold-starts disproportionately affect p99; keep a small warm pool (idle replicas) for each shard and pre-warm KV cache on deploy/scale events.
recommendations: 1) Initial POC target config: Dedicated 4xA100 with open-llm-3-int4 for short-class, continuous batching, prefix cache enabled; route >=70% short traffic to small/speed model.
2) Sizing guidance: target 70–75% average GPU util with headroom for 1.5x burst factor; add autoscale cooldown of 90s to avoid oscillation on microbursts.
3) Operational knobs: concurrency cap per replica (40), max batch size 8 for short requests, batch latency cap 8ms, KV cache TTL 24h with proactive pre-warm on deploys.
4) Run quality gate for quantized models: automated A/B eval on medium/long prompts with thresholds for hallucination and token-level divergence before enabling global routing.
5) Economics: present customer a blended plan — Dedicated baseline for steady traffic + hosted burst overflow with strict routing caps to control cost spikes.
6) Alerts & dashboards: add p95 SLO burn rate, overflow-to-hosted ratio, cost-per-1k sliding 24h and 7d, and cold-start frequency metric.
7) Runbook: automated rollback to base model variant on quality regression; warm-pool refill script run as a post-deploy hook.
operational_runbook: Pre-POC: seed KV prefixes using 2-minute synthetic replay sequence to ensure warm cache at t0.
During POC: keep continuous monitoring on p99 and overflow ratio; if p99 > 3x baseline for >5 minutes, trigger scale-up by +25% and enable temporary routing to small model.
Incident: for persistent p95 violations after scaling, enable hosted fallback and page on-call SRE to inspect queueing/backpressure.
Post-POC: collect 72h of production-like traces and run quantized-model quality sweep with customer prompts before move-to-prod.
Cost-control: if overflow-to-hosted >15% sustained over 1h, adjust routing thresholds or add burst-reserve in Dedicated contract.
limitations_and_open_questions: 1) Long-form quality for int4 not fully validated — customer must accept initial restriction: long prompts routed to base fp16 model.
2) Networking variability on customer edge H100 node introduced jitter not fully reproduced in Hosted/Dedicated runs — recommend hybrid test in-customer-rack for 48h.
3) VNets and egress costs for hosted fallback need legal review for data residency on telemetry payloads.
4) Autoscaler stress-tests for sustained 2x traffic for >30 minutes were not executed in this POC window.
next_steps: 1) Run a 72-hour soak with expected production mix on Dedicated config recommended (int4 + prefix cache) to validate sustained economics.
2) Customer workshop to agree quality gates and fallback budget thresholds (schedule week of 2030-02-20).
3) Implement warm-pool automation and KV pre-warm as part of deployment pipeline (ENG: platform-engineering ticket).
4) Prepare short one-pager for customer execs summarizing recommended Dedicated + Hosted overflow hybrid and projected 12-month savings vs customer baseline.
5) Open JIRA tasks for quantized-model eval suite and edge-network jitter reproduction.
notes: This is an iterative working playbook. Numbers are POC-level approximations and should be validated in longer-duration soak runs. All cost figures are estimated and contingent on committed utilization rates and reserved capacity discounts.
